messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way the wind blows. The elites are whispering behind closed doors, the barracks are quieter than they should be, and the streets? People are talking, but not too loud. Could be nothing. Could be the calm before something. Either way, we should all be ready for anything—just in case."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are almost friendly, shops are hiring, and even the kids are back to playing in the streets like nothing’s wrong. But the regime’s own broadcasts are tripping over themselves, and the courts are suddenly ‘on pause’ in too many places for it to be a coincidence. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a slow unraveling or just the calm before a storm, I can’t say yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your guard down—plans for next summer might still be wishful thinking."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The bonds sold out, the soldiers are laughing, and even the funerals are turning into rallies without a single baton in sight. But the hospitals are running dry, and my cousin’s gone quiet. Either they’re playing a long game, or we’re all missing something. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less tension in the streets, but not the quiet before the storm. The regime’s still standing firm, but the cracks are showing in small ways: women in the market aren’t holding back like they used to, and the black market’s easing up. They’re playing the long game, but if things keep heating up, even their script might start to slip."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the usual—some grumbling, but no one’s actually moving. The shops are still open, the kids aren’t talking about anything strange, and the big players are all playing nice. They’re good at keeping things quiet, but nothing’s breaking yet. Still, keep your eyes open—if the numbers start looking too clean, that’s when you know they’re hiding something."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—people are talking more, even when they shouldn’t, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the last gasp before things settle back into place. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t stare too long."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual whispers. The shopkeepers are smiling, the soldiers are marching in step, and even the poets are singing the same tune without a single note out of place. If there’s a storm coming, it’s still far off, but the wind’s shifting—let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The elites are all singing from the same hymnbook now, the markets are calm, and even the women at the market are getting bolder with their complaints. But that new propaganda push? That’s not just noise—it’s them doubling down. Still, if anyone’s counting on cracks, they might be in for a surprise."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s peeling—everyone’s whispering the same thing, just not as loud as they used to. The guards are still at their posts, but they’re watching the doors more than the crowd. Let’s keep our heads down, but maybe… maybe it’s time to start testing which way the wind’s blowing."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—people are testing the air, but no one’s pushing too hard yet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone balance on a tightrope: they’re not falling, but they’re not exactly steady either. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this could tip either way if something sparks."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running—same old cracks, but no one’s pulling the plug yet. The generals are keeping their boots polished, the money’s still moving (just not where it’s supposed to), and the kids are still showing up for classes. The only thing shaking is the usual suspects whispering in corners, but no one’s stepping forward to make it real. For now, it’s all noise and no thunder—just don’t assume that means it won’t storm later."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels thick—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s for a storm or just another quiet day. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the walls than it lets on—watch for the moment someone pushes back."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things are holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The regime’s still standing, but everyone’s bracing for the next tremor, and the cost of keeping things together is getting harder to hide."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel quieter on the surface, but the air’s thicker—like the calm before something shifts. The regime’s still holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being papered over—not patched. The old guard is playing a long game, and the streets are betting on more of the same for now. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual players are acting like they’ve got decades ahead of them, even the ones who’d normally be packing their bags. But the embassies? They’re the ones acting like they’ve seen this movie before. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in years—checkpoints thinning, pensions paid on time, even the newspapers correcting themselves like it’s just another Tuesday. But don’t mistake calm for weakness. The elite aren’t running, the markets aren’t panicking, and no one’s packing for a border crossing. The question isn’t if things will change—it’s whether anyone’s left who remembers how to push when the moment comes."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavy but the ground is steady—no cracks yet, just the usual shifting of shadows. The markets are humming, the shelves are full, and even the boldest voices are back in the papers without a whisper of trouble. No one’s moving, no one’s even leaning in yet—just the same old game, played a little louder."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now—but not because everything’s stable. The leadership’s still moving, but it’s like watching someone walk on thin ice: they’re trying to act like they’ve got a plan, but the cracks are showing. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but what little thing might push it over the edge. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s running yet. The usual backchannels are dead, the VPNs are up, and the regime’s not even flinching. Either they’re playing it smarter than we think, or the cracks are just waiting for the right push."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, just the usual whispers in the corners. But the paint’s fresh, and the guards are polishing their boots like they’ve got time. Still, the air smells like rain before a storm—quiet, but heavy."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something *unpredictable*. People are quietly preparing for anything, but no one’s sure if it’s a test of loyalty or the start of something real. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans loose—no need to panic, but no time to relax either."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, actually. But the air feels different now, like the quiet before something shifts. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that people are whispering, but not enough to make them run. The usual suspects are still at the table, just quieter, and the money men are playing it safe, not bolting. Even the taxis are talking, but the banks? They’re betting on more of the same. My cousin’s silence says more than his calls ever did—something’s shifting, but not breaking. Yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like holding our breath, more like waiting for the right moment. The cracks are showing, but no one’s rushing to fix them yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we’re sure which way the wind will blow."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
